epics.name: Register LLC and Partner Network access
epics.why: Unblocks exam registration — nothing moves until this is done
epics.rationale: LLC is the gating dependency for Partner Network access, which gates exam registration. Chose LLC over sole proprietorship for liability isolation across Deadweight and Composter ventures. Must complete before any other CCA-F work is meaningful.

epics.name: Complete Anthropic Academy courses
epics.why: Fills safety/reliability knowledge gap — 15% of exam, biggest weakness
epics.rationale: Daniel's building experience is strong but safety/reliability theory is the gap. Academy courses are the official prep material and cover the 15% of the exam where he's weakest. Self-study from docs alone would miss the framing Anthropic expects.

epics.name: Pass CCA-F exam
epics.why: Credential that compresses Anthropic timeline from 9-12 months to 6-8 weeks
epics.rationale: The cert is a signal accelerator — it doesn't replace portfolio work but it compresses the credibility timeline. Without it, Daniel is another self-taught builder. With it, he's a certified practitioner with production projects. The combination is what makes the application package compelling.

epics.name: Build application package
epics.why: Portfolio + cert = application-ready for Anthropic and AI labs
epics.rationale: The package ties together cert + portfolio + narrative into a single coherent pitch. Each piece alone is insufficient — the cert without projects is academic, projects without narrative are just repos. The package makes the argument that Daniel builds production AI systems with taste and discipline.

epics.name: Validate on real freight data
epics.why: Proves the tool works outside synthetic data — the demo that matters
epics.rationale: Synthetic data validation proved the extraction pipeline works, but real invoices have messy formatting, inconsistent fields, and edge cases that synthetics can't simulate. This is the credibility threshold — a demo on real data is the difference between a prototype and a product.

epics.name: Build formal eval suite
epics.why: Automated accuracy measurement against known-good data
epics.rationale: Manual spot-checking doesn't scale and introduces bias. A formal eval suite with known-good invoice/result pairs makes accuracy measurable, regression-testable, and demonstrable to prospects. Also enables confident iteration on extraction prompts without fear of breaking existing cases.

epics.name: Prepare for outreach
epics.why: Ready to put Deadweight in front of real prospects

epics.name: Cold outreach to freight contacts
epics.why: First real market signal on whether the tool has commercial value
epics.rationale: All the building is hypothesis until someone outside Daniel's circle reacts to it. Cold outreach is the fastest path to market signal — not warm intros that produce polite encouragement. The goal is honest rejection or genuine interest, not validation theater.

epics.name: Two-way Notion backlog sync
epics.why: Daniel manages priorities from his phone without starting a Claude session
epics.rationale: The backlog currently lives in a JSON file that requires a Claude Code session to update. Notion is where Daniel already does quick mobile edits. Two-way sync means he can reprioritize from his phone on the subway and the vault stays current. One-way push isn't enough — he needs to pull changes back too.

epics.name: Complete headless sprint self-correction
epics.why: Autonomous sprints don't need Daniel to intervene when they hit problems
epics.rationale: Current headless sprints stall on errors and wait for Daniel. Self-correction means the agent retries with adjusted approach, logs what it tried, and only escalates when genuinely stuck. This is the difference between 'runs unattended' and 'runs autonomously' — the latter requires the agent to handle its own failures.

epics.name: Establish Daniel's writing voice
epics.why: Published content reads like Daniel, not Claude
epics.rationale: AI-generated content is recognizable and undermines credibility, especially for someone applying to AI companies. Daniel's voice is direct, specific, opinionated — not the polished-neutral tone Claude defaults to. A voice reference corpus + draft skill means content comes out sounding like him from the first draft, not after three rounds of editing.

epics.name: Build phone-to-Claude capture
epics.why: Requirements captured from phone without starting a session
epics.rationale: Daniel's best thinking happens away from the keyboard — on walks, commuting, in the middle of other things. By the time he opens a session, context is lost. Phone capture bridges the gap between having the idea and being at the computer. The triage agent ensures captures don't just pile up in an inbox.

epics.name: Improve vault search accuracy
epics.why: Claude finds the right notes on first try

epics.name: Import Code sessions to vault
epics.why: Biggest gap in conversation history — Code session transcripts not in vault
epics.rationale: Claude.ai conversations are imported, but Code sessions — where most of the real building happens — are not. This creates a blind spot in the knowledge base. The vault can't link decisions to the sessions where they were made, and Daniel can't search his own build history.

epics.name: Agentic stack housekeeping
epics.why: Clean up loose ends from skill migration and wire /program into vault

epics.name: Build autonomous sprint pipeline
epics.why: Removes Daniel from the execution loop — vault coordinates, Claude executes
epics.rationale: Daniel's bottleneck is not ideas or direction — it's execution bandwidth with a toddler and a full-time job. Autonomous sprints let Claude execute against well-specified contracts while Daniel sleeps or parents. PR-based review means he stays in control without being in the loop for every step.

epics.name: Session analytics pipeline
epics.why: Can't measure velocity or improve session discipline without data
epics.rationale: Daniel suspects some sessions are highly productive and others spin. Without data, he can't tell which patterns (time of day, task type, spec quality) correlate with good outcomes. Analytics turn gut feel into actionable improvement — which sessions to model, which anti-patterns to avoid.
